question: E205 priced a per-factor IC sign; E208 priced all 64 vectors on one window. The operator's actual procedure is neither: pick one vector from history and run it. Does trailing-Sharpe re-selection of the 64 vectors earn anything point-in-time, on the declared cells, against the equal-weight control?

arms.BEST: the best of the 64 vectors on this window (in-sample oracle)
arms.CONTROL: equal weight across the whole eligible universe, same cadence
arms.PIT: trailing-Sharpe winner of the 64, re-picked every `reselect` bars

declared.exit_axis: strategy_own_exit (rebalance turnover only; engine default exit stack unused)
declared.selection_space: 2^6 sign vectors, 6 PIT variants x 2 cells = 12 declared tests

caveats: Both oracle arms (PROD, BEST) are in-sample by construction: their signs were read off this panel (E205/E208). Only the PIT arms are candidates for a live claim.
The PIT arm here re-selects a VECTOR; E205 re-signed each FACTOR from its own IC. They are different procedures and their numbers are not interchangeable.
Selection is by trailing Sharpe over the declared lookback only; no other statistic was swept, so the variant grid is 3x2 and not an optimised surface.
The reference engine charges 10bp/side and ignores impact and gap risk; the equal-weight control runs the same engine and cadence, so the comparison is paired.
ETF pool is today's listed set (survivorship); all cells are one panel, one cost level.

checks.check: every declared variant present in every cell
every variant has events and only declared picks
beat/positive flags recomputed from published cagr
verdict recomputed from the variant table
at least one variant was measured
